title: Build TaskFlow Lite in JavaScript
goal: Turn the static page into a working task manager using only browser JavaScript so the language fundamentals are visible.
steps: Model one task as a plain object, then create an array of tasks.
Write pure functions for creating, updating, filtering, and deleting tasks.
Render the array into the DOM and keep rendering separate from state-changing functions.
Wire form submit and button events to the state functions.
Add search and status filtering as derived values rather than duplicate state.
Persist tasks to localStorage and safely handle missing or malformed stored JSON.
Add an async request with `fetch`, loading/error handling, and cancellation.
Introduce one race or stale-result bug, then fix it deliberately.
Reload the page and prove all expected behavior still works.
evidence: A clean Git diff or file-tree change
Browser, HTTP, database, test, container, or CI evidence that proves the behavior
One deliberate failure, the evidence you used, and the root-cause fix
A short explanation of why the final responsibility lives in the chosen layer
completion: I can reproduce one key part without the walkthrough.
I can explain one trade-off I deliberately chose.
I can show one failure that my tests, constraints, or runbook now protects against.
